{{distinguish|Sierpiński space}}
In mathematics, a '''Sierpiński set''' is an [[uncountable]] subset of a [[real vector space]] whose intersection with every [[measure-zero set]] is countable. The existence of Sierpiński sets is independent of the axioms of [[ZFC]]. {{harvs|txt|last=Sierpiński|year=1924|authorlink=Wacław Sierpiński}} showed that they exist if the [[continuum hypothesis]] is true.  On the other hand, they do not exist if [[Martin's axiom]] for ℵ<sub>1</sub> is true. Sierpiński sets are weakly Luzin sets but are not [[Luzin set]]s {{harv|Kunen|2011|loc=p. 376}}.

==Example of a Sierpiński set==

Choose a collection of 2<sup>ℵ<sub>0</sub></sup> measure-0 subsets of '''R''' such that every measure-0 subset is contained in one of them. By the continuum hypothesis, it is possible to enumerate them as ''S''<sub>''α''</sub> for countable ordinals ''α''. For each countable ordinal ''β'' choose a real number ''x''<sub>''β''</sub> that is not in any of the sets ''S''<sub>''α''</sub> for ''α''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''β'', which is possible as the union of these sets has measure 0 so is not the whole of '''R'''. Then the uncountable set ''X'' of all these real numbers ''x''<sub>''β''</sub> has only a countable number of elements in each set ''S''<sub>''α''</sub>, so is a Sierpiński set.

It is possible for a Sierpiński set to be a [[subgroup]] under addition. For this one modifies the construction above by choosing a real number ''x''<sub>''β''</sub> that is not in any of the countable number of sets of the form (''S''<sub>''α''</sub>&nbsp;+&nbsp;''X'')/''n'' for ''α''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''β'', where ''n'' is a positive integer and ''X'' is an integral linear combination of the numbers ''x''<sub>''α''</sub> for ''α''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''β''. Then the group generated by these numbers is a Sierpiński set and a group under addition. More complicated variations of this construction produce examples of Sierpiński sets that are [[field extension|subfield]]s or [[real-closed field|real-closed subfield]]s of the real numbers.
